components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Teal action: the main thing to do on a screen.

narrative.overview:
ColdChain is built from label stock. Cool white panels sit on a pale slate ground like adhesive labels on a fridge door, cut with a small die-cut corner and edged by a single 1px slate rule. Teal ink marks what you can act on and where you are; everything else stays quiet slate so that status can be loud when it has to be.

Status is read the way a nurse reads a vaccine vial monitor: a square inside a circle, the square darkening as the heat budget is used. That mark is both the logo and the status glyph, and every status in the product travels as colour plus mark plus word. The density is operational: a clinic PC and a night-shift wall monitor, desktop first, still whole at 360px. Light and dark are one system with remapped values; dark exists for the wall monitor, not as a mood.

The world refuses the generic IoT dashboard: no grid of KPI cards with sparklines standing in for state.
keyCharacteristics: Label-stock panels on a slate ground, 1px rules, 6px die-cut corners.
Teal is the only action and selection ink; status inks never double as actions.
Every status is colour + VVM mark + word, never colour alone.
One workhorse face, Public Sans, with tabular figures for readings.
Calm at rest; motion only when a status actually changes.

rules.name: The Three-Signal Rule
rules.body: A status is never colour alone: it is the status ink, the VVM mark (or a distinct lucide glyph for connection state), and a word. Where width forces the word out, it moves to `sr-only`, not away.

rules.name: The Teal-Is-Action Rule
rules.body: Teal means "act here" or "you are here". It never signals a status, and status inks never fill a primary action except Breach Red on a destructive confirm.

rules.name: The Wash Pairing Rule
rules.body: Status ink sits on its own wash (chips) or on a 9 % mix of the ink into panel (the global status pill), with a border of the ink at 35 to 40 % opacity. Every ink-on-wash pair holds 4.5:1 or better in both themes.

rules.name: The Violet Disclosure Rule
rules.body: Disclosure Violet appears only on the demo-mode banner, full width, above the top bar, on every screen while time is accelerated.

rules.name: The One Workhorse Rule
rules.body: Public Sans is the only family. Readings, counts, lot numbers and alert counts use tabular figures (`.figures`) so columns and live numbers do not jitter.

rules.name: The Label-On-Surface Rule
rules.body: Resting surfaces get the hairline label lift and nothing heavier; only things that float above the page (menus, toasts, dialogs) get diffuse shadows. No hard offset shadows.

rules.name: The Die-Cut Rule
rules.body: Containers and controls are 6px, status is round. Nothing in between, nothing sharper, nothing softer.

rules.name: The Strike Rule
rules.body: DISCARD is permanent and looks crossed out: a -45° repeating strike (2px ink at 16 % every 7px) over its wash, and the diagonal cut in its mark.

rules.name: The Pulse-On-Change Rule
rules.body: Motion is a signal: the only attention motion is the single VVM pulse on a real status change. Reduced motion collapses all animation to 1ms.

dos: Do put every status through the shared vocabulary: status ink + VVM mark + word, from one source of truth.
Do use Monitor Teal for primary actions, selection, focus and the logo, and only for those.
Do keep containers and controls at the 6px die-cut corner and status shapes fully round.
Do set readings, counts and lot numbers in tabular figures.
Do show the demo-mode banner in Disclosure Violet on every screen whenever heat exposure is accelerated.
Do show connection state (live, polling, connecting) with a distinct glyph per state, plus the word from sm up.
Do strike DISCARD with the diagonal pattern wherever it appears.
donts: Don't build the generic IoT dashboard of KPI cards and sparklines; state is read from VVM marks and words.
Don't signal status with colour alone, or with teal.
Don't pulse or animate the VVM mark on mount, on route change, or on a loop.
Don't use hard offset shadows or anything heavier than the label lift on resting surfaces.
Don't use the modal for anything but protected-focus confirmations; everything else stays inline.
